chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of three men who had intercourse with a woman during one period of purity, and this was in the pre-Islamic era before the emergence of Islam. He cast lots among them and assigned the child to the one whose lot was drawn, and placed two-thirds of the blood money on the other two. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) laughed until his incisors became visible, and said: 'I know nothing about it except what Ali ruled.' So these two reports do not contradict the earlier reports, because the explanation in them is that if the girl was shared between two or three men and they all had intercourse with her during one period of purity, the ruling was by casting lots. And the earlier reports only stipulated that the child belongs to the one who possesses the girl, when she was changing ownership.

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: the girl/woman (often implying a slave or concubine in this context)

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined when multiple men have intercourse with a shared woman in one period of purity?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the practical jurisprudence of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) in resolving paternity disputes among multiple partners through casting lots (qur'a), a method validated by the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) laughter and approval. The text reconciles this with other hadiths by distinguishing between shared ownership, where lots determine lineage, and exclusive ownership, where the child belongs to the owner, demonstrating the flexibility of Shia legal reasoning in pre-Islamic and early Islamic contexts.
